tasks.title: Identify the Alert
tasks.prompt: What is the alert ID reported by the secure email gateway? Enter the identifier exactly as shown in the alert.
hints: The gateway alert is captured in case/alert.json.
Look at the `alert_id` field.

tasks.title: Extract Sender Identity
tasks.prompt: What is the From email address of the message (the address, not the display name)?
hints: See case/email_headers.json.
The display name and the actual address are different things — report the address.

tasks.title: Inspect Reply-To Mismatch
tasks.prompt: Does the Reply-To domain align with the From domain?
hints: Compare the From and Reply-To domains.
Look at where a reply would actually be delivered.

tasks.title: Evaluate Authentication Results
tasks.prompt: What is the DMARC result for this message?
hints: Authentication results live in case/email_headers.json.
Remember SPF pass alone does not imply DMARC pass — alignment matters.

tasks.title: Detect Lookalike Domain
tasks.prompt: Enter the sender domain that imitates a trusted domain (the lookalike domain).
hints: Compare the From domain against reference/trusted_domains.json.
Watch for a digit used in place of a letter.

tasks.title: Build Header Finding
tasks.prompt: Select every header-based red flag supported by the evidence.
hints: A red flag is an indicator consistent with impersonation.
SPF passing is not itself a red flag — focus on alignment, Reply-To, and the sender domain.

tasks.title: Extract the Primary URL
tasks.prompt: Enter the primary URL from the email body, in its defanged form, exactly as written.
hints: The URL is in case/email_body.txt.
Keep it defanged — do not re-fang hxxps or [.].

tasks.title: Identify URL Red Flags
tasks.prompt: Select every URL red flag supported by the evidence.
hints: Check the host domain against the trusted domain list.
Consider what the path is luring the user to do; note that TLS alone is not a safety signal.

tasks.title: Inspect Attachment Metadata
tasks.prompt: Does the attachment's declared content type match its observed content type?
hints: See case/attachment_manifest.json.
Compare declared_content_type with observed_content_type.

tasks.title: Verify File Hash
tasks.prompt: Enter the SHA-256 of the attachment as recorded in the manifest.
hints: See the `sha256` field in case/attachment_manifest.json.
A SHA-256 is 64 hexadecimal characters.

tasks.title: Correlate Gateway Events
tasks.prompt: To how many recipients was this message delivered, according to the gateway events?
hints: See case/gateway_events.jsonl.
Count distinct recipients with a message_delivered event for this message_id.

tasks.title: Determine User Exposure
tasks.prompt: What is the furthest level of user exposure reached across all recipients?
hints: Correlate the gateway, mailbox, and proxy logs.
Check whether any click occurred and whether it was blocked or led to credential submission.

tasks.title: Build Incident Timeline
tasks.prompt: Order every event_id (across gateway, mailbox, and proxy logs) from earliest to latest by timestamp.
hints: Collect events from all three logs.
Sort strictly by the ISO 8601 timestamp.

tasks.title: Assess Credential Risk
tasks.prompt: What is the credential-harvesting outcome supported by the evidence?
hints: A click occurred — check what happened next in the proxy log.
Look at the action and credential_submission indicator.

tasks.title: Determine Severity
hints: Weigh confirmed phishing and a click against the fact that it was blocked with no credential submission.
Do not default to high without supporting exposure.

tasks.title: Select Incident Verdict
hints: Weigh the combined header, URL, attachment, and exposure evidence.
A confirmed impersonation with a malicious lure is not merely suspicious.

tasks.title: Recommend Containment Actions
tasks.prompt: Select the proportionate containment / escalation actions.
hints: Choose actions proportionate to a blocked click with no credential submission.
Avoid disproportionate actions that would disrupt the whole organization.

tasks.title: Submit Final Triage Report
tasks.prompt: Submit the structured final triage report. Required fields: case_id, verdict, severity, confidence, user_exposure, key_evidence (list), recommended_actions (list), rationale.
hints: Reuse your answers from the verdict, severity, and exposure tasks.
key_evidence should name the concrete indicators you relied on.
